Home News Arts and Culture Business Sports Opinion Research Live TV/Radio Media Elections Dark Mode Dark mode --> Education ‘Teach her, don’t touch her’ – Women in PR Ghana joins fight against sexual abuse in schools Source : Myjoyonline.com 26 November 2026 10:32am ▶ Listen to this article Audio By Carbonatix
Women in PR Ghana has intensified calls for stronger protection of girls against sexual harassment and abuse in schools, endorsing a national campaign to make educational and professional spaces safer.
The professional body has backed the “Teach Her, Don’t Touch Her” campaign, an initiative by the Aya Institute for Women, Politics, and Media.
The endorsement comes as the world marks the International Day for the Elimination of Violence Against Women.
The campaign seeks to combat sexual violence through prevention, protection and institutional accountability.
As part of its support, Women in PR Ghana has established a Communications Advisory Committee to strengthen the campaign’s messaging, public education and advocacy.
The committee will draw on the expertise and professional networks of its members to amplify the campaign, challenge harmful attitudes and raise awareness of sexual harassment and abuse.
The initiative comes amid renewed public concern over sexual abuse in educational institutions, including a reported case involving a student of Obuasi Senior High Technical School (SHTS).
The case has heightened concerns about safeguarding gaps within the education sector and the need for stronger institutional mechanisms to prevent abuse and handle complaints.
It has also reinforced calls for safe reporting systems that allow students to seek help without fear, stigma or retaliation.
President of Women in PR Ghana, Josephine Appiah-Nyamekye Sanny, said protecting girls requires action beyond public condemnation of incidents of abuse.
“Sexual harassment and abuse of girls must never be normalised, excused or silenced.
“Protecting girls requires more than public outrage when incidents occur; it requires deliberate education, clear safeguards, accountability and a collective commitment to changing the attitudes and behaviours that enable abuse,” she said.
She stressed that communication professionals have a critical role to play in confronting harmful social norms and advancing the protection of vulnerable girls.
“As communication professionals, we have a responsibility to use our skills and platforms to advance issues that matter.
“Our endorsement of this campaign and the establishment of the Communications Advisory Committee reflect our commitment to lending our expertise to efforts that empower girls, encourage safe reporting and help create environments where their safety and dignity are respected,” she added.
Women in PR Ghana also commended the Aya Institute for spearheading the campaign and bringing institutions, professionals and communities together to confront sexual abuse.
Through the partnership, the organisation hopes to harness strategic communication to challenge harmful attitudes, strengthen public awareness and promote collective responsibility for the safety and dignity of girls and young women.
